title: Signal Zoetrope — customer threads & feature seeds (rapid synth)
content:
Purpose
Quick, loose synthesis of customer threads collected Mar 8–Mar 21. Focused on runtime friction and small-to-medium feature seeds that reduce customer operational load or unblock higher usage. Not a final roadmap — this is a field notebook for product + eng to triage.

Context and signal summary (topline)
- Several mid-market customers reporting repeated "cold-start" tail latency spikes when traffic bursts after idle windows. Not all on same model; pattern correlates with small sustained burst traffic and model-initialization on Dedicated pools.
- Multi-tenant customers asking for "per-route SLA overrides" — ability to promote particular API keys/routes to a higher priority within a single Dedicated cluster (fine-grained routing).
- Recurrent ask: more transparent KV/prefix cache stats visible in Console (per-tenant hit-rate, prefix-distribution, bytes saved). Customers say current visibility is opaque and makes troubleshooting caching regressions slow.
- A cluster of requests for embedding throughput contracts and bulk-embedding job primitives (async bulk jobs with progress hooks).
- A few customers flagged token billing discrepancies vs their internal meter — mostly related to streaming/resume interactions and trimmed control tokens.

Representative customer vignettes
1) FinSearch (mid-market, search+rerank): observed 700ms tail spikes after low-traffic hours. They want an "instance warm" option for scheduled jobs and shorter cold-start TTLs to be configurable per model variant.
2) LegalAI (enterprise, private deployment): needs per-route priority because teams share a single Dedicated cluster; finance team workloads must never be throttled by product experiments. Asking for routing/priority UI and API.
3) Recommendation retail customer: needs bulk-embedding exports to S3 with hooks (start/complete webhooks) and ability to resume failed batches without re-embedding whole file.

Concrete feature seeds (ranked by expected customer impact / engineering ease)
A. Console: Prefix Cache Snapshot (M) — show per-keyspace hit-rate, top-100 prefixes, evictions, and estimated $/day saved. Add a simple "capture sample prefix" button to reproduce reported cases. (Est 2–3 sprint eng work + product UI)
B. Dedicated: Route Priority Tagging (M-L) — annotation on API key/routes with priority weight; scheduler treats high-priority traffic as reserved tokens/bandwidth. Start with soft-priority + metrics, then add hard-reservation later. (Est 3–5 sprints infra + SRE)
C. Embeddings: Bulk Job API (M) — async job primitive: upload list, start job, incremental progress, checkpointed resume, output to S3/GC. Consider costs per-100k vectors and retry semantics. (Est 2–4 sprints infra + SDK)
D. Billing: Streaming token reconciliation tooling (S) — a Console diagnostic mode that replays streaming session events vs billing records and highlights mismatches. (Est 1 sprint + small data infra)
E. Dedicated: Scheduled Warm (S) — per-model "keep-warm" schedule that pins minimal capacity during specified windows (lighter than full reservation). Useful for predictable daily bursts. (Est 1–2 sprints)
F. SDK: Streaming resume examples + canonical patterns (XS) — document patterns and add sample code for resume/trim handling to reduce billing mismatches. (Docs + 1 sprint engineering docs)

Tradeoffs / risk notes
- Route Priority (B) requires careful allocation logic to avoid noisy-neighbor priority inversion; start with monitoring-only release to validate policy before hard-reserving.
- Prefix Cache Snapshot could expose internal memory usage semantics; need privacy check for multi-tenant keyspace names. Data shown should be aggregated/hashed where appropriate.
- Bulk embedding jobs create operational load spikes; gate via quotas and recommend batch windowing.

Unresolved questions for product/infra
- For "keep-warm": should we make it a tiny reserved capacity (billing as minimal Dedicated commit) or a transient scheduling hint (no billing change)? Customers expect guaranteed lower tail latency, so billing model matters. Input from pricing needed.
- What is the acceptable retention window for per-route priority metrics in Console (30d, 90d)? Longer retention increases storage cost.
- For embeddings resume semantics: do we support idempotent vectorization keys or rely on chunked checkpoints? Engineering preference?

Quick action items / who-does-what
- CS: validate priority asks with LegalAI and 2 other enterprise customers, capture exact SLA language they want. Owner: Aisha (due 2026-03-29).
- Eng infra: spike feasibility for Route Priority with simulated traffic model (JIRA RED-4823). Owner: Rajat (due 2026-04-06).
- Product: draft pricing options for "Scheduled Warm" (minimal reserve vs hint) and propose default for Dedicated customers. Owner: Jonah (due 2026-04-02).
- DevRel: add a short streaming+billing reconciliation recipe to docs and sample code repo (PR to come: github.com/redwood/prs/pull/2378). Owner: Lena (due 2026-03-31).

Notes from support threads (raw, lightly edited)
- "We saw a jump in 95th from 110ms to 860ms after midnight — reads as cold-start. Is there a way to keep a hot standby for our prime model?" — FinSearch support ticket #45312
- "We share a dedicated cluster across 6 teams. If one team runs heavy training-style batch calls it kills our synchronous APIs. We need a route-level priority we can set via Console or API." — LegalAI account exec
- "Embedding bulk loads fail ~4% through file; when we restart the job it either re-runs from start or we hack offsets client-side. Need checkpoint resume." — RetailRec engineering

Bridge to existing work
- Prefix/KV cache workstream (serving-runtime): there is an internal spike scheduled for Apr where eng looks at eviction telemetry. We should sync on Console requirements so the UI can consume the same telemetry. Linked: CONFLUENCE:INFERENCE-ops-cache-playbook-9812.
- Dedicated scheduler refactor roadmap (infra): relevant for route-priority; schedule sync requested with infra leads.

Quick prototype sketches (notes to eng)
- Cache UI: heatmap with per-route toggle, overlay estimated savings line. Option to export top-keys CSV. Hash-sensitive keys masked by default.
- Route Priority: soft-weight model where each route has weight w in [0.1,10]. The scheduler multiplies available concurrency by weight fraction and reports expected throttles. Start by exposing in Console as "priority tuning" with no enforcement.
- Bulk embeddings: chunk-size default 10k vectors, checkpoint every chunk to multipart S3. Job metadata stores client-supplied idempotency key.

Success metrics (how customers will know we solved it)
- Tail latency post-warm: 95th drops by >=40% for warm-scheduled customers in first 30 days.
- Support ticket reduction: fewer repeat cold-start tickets for customers who enabled scheduled warm. Target: -60% repeat tickets month-over-month.
- Cache visibility adoption: 20 customers using Prefix Cache Snapshot within 60 days and reporting actionable findings.
- Bulk embedding: mean time to completion for 1M vectors improved by 15% vs current ad-hoc jobs and restart rate <1%.

Open for review
Please add notes inline (this is a working doc). If you own a listed action, update status in the doc or in RED-4823. Next field sync: 2026-04-06 10:00 PT (30m).

Raw links and tickets (for triage)
- RED-4823 (route-priority spike)
- Support#45312 (FinSearch cold-start)
- RetailRec-embed-fail (internal ticket id 8921)
- CONFLUENCE:INFERENCE-ops-cache-playbook-9812
- GitHub pr: github.com/redwood/inference-docs/pull/2378

End of rapid synth — Aisha
